title: bondcell's bonded membrane rings are not self-maintaining: fed or starved they decay at the membrane turnover rate, and starvation does not single them out
summary: Follow-up to 20261025T0936-c05-bonded-membrane-rings and the question 20261025T1030-c05-q-bondcell-starve-divide, at half size and equal density (N=2000, L=11.31; world_small.py, no-bond twin world_small_nobond.py), seed 0. Each world was run to t=60 and branched into a fed arm and a starved arm (k_cat=k_cat1=0: food can no longer become core), to t=140 (starve.py; sb.log, sn.log; starve_fork.png). Bonded fed arm: membrane M 167 -> 112 -> 76 (bonds 156 -> 71) while core C grows 1306 -> 1531; at t=140 only 2 of ~7 dense cores still carry a closed ring, the rest are bare loose clusters. Bonded starved arm: M 167 -> 119 -> 83, C 1306 -> 552; by t=140 one ringed dense core remains as a body and the loose clusters have dissolved. No-bond twin: fed M 2 -> 0 (bare cores); starved M 2 -> 81 -> 95, because shrinking cores re-expose food-facing surfaces and the parent's food-conditional rule makes membrane again (orange rims on most cores at t=100-140). So bonds keep a ring only for about the membrane lifetime (k_mdec=0.01, ~100 t) and do not renew it: renewal needs surface conversion, which the monolayer rule (m_lim=4) and food depletion suppress.

finding.operator: harmonic chain bonds between membrane particles (bondcell)
finding.control: fed vs starved fork at t=60 from the same state; bonds=0 twin forked the same way
finding.result: bonded M 167 -> 76 fed and -> 83 starved over t=60-140 (2 of ~7 rings left fed, 1 ringed core left starved); no-bond M 2 -> 0 fed but 2 -> 95 starved (food-conditional rims return)
